project.name: Silver Ridge Railway
project.character: Practical shortline, not tourist railroad tone
project.interchange_partner: Denver & Rio Grande Western (D&RGW). Original Class I partner since SRRX founding 1904. D&RGW founded 1870. Do not change or confuse this.
project.pvj_note: PVJ = Pine Valley Junction. Never 'Port Vance Junction' or any other expansion. Do not confuse or hallucinate alternate names.

locations.PVJ_industrial_spur: South side of PVJ, light blue on V8. Labeled "PVJ Depot and Intermodal" in V8 legend. Serves warehouse and passenger depot. Branches independently from mainline with NO connection to yard ladder.
locations.team_track_RIP: Gray track at south end of yard ladder. Passive/multipurpose. Absorbed into yard protection zone.
locations.mine_branch: Grade-intensive spur with switchback grades ascending to mine
locations.helper_pocket: Staging for helper engines on mine ascents. Part of PVJ yard protection zone.
locations.tunnel_bores: Two bores through the mountain. Part of north leg.
locations.gorge: East leg, south of the mountain
locations.southern_tunnel_portals: Boundary between north and south halves of layout
locations.smelter: Industry spur, part of mine run

geography.orientation: North leg = PVJ side through tunnels. South of mountain = Silver Ridge side, gorge, east leg.

rivers.pine_river: Runs through Pine Valley District and PVJ area. Named the valley (Pine Valley) before the railroad arrived.
rivers.elk_river: Runs through Silver Ridge District and gorge country. Drains the Elk River Valley. Replaces 'Silver Ridge River' everywhere.

geography.valley: Elk River Valley - the broader geographic region the SRRX operates in. Two river systems: Pine River (north/PVJ) and Elk River (south/Silver Ridge). The SRRX links two separate drainages across a mountain divide.

acquisitions.status: In hand and in active use as of 2026-06-08
acquisitions.notes: Entry-level. Current nozzle: 0.3mm. Also have 0.2mm and 0.5mm sets. First test ~2026-05-25: too thin, tape bleed. Tamiya low-tack tape needed. 2026-06-07 session: brick red on Federal Building worked well. Metallic silver for fencing clogged the 0.3mm nozzle - metallic pigment particles lodged in tip even after cleaning. Nozzle passed air and water but pulsed under back-pressure. Diagnosis: partial metallic clog in nozzle tip. Fix: soak 0.3mm nozzle assembly in airbrush cleaner overnight. RULE: never use metallic paint through 0.3mm. Use 0.5mm for metallics and large body areas (caboose body next). Use airbrush medium not water for thinning metallics. Never stop flow mid-session without flushing immediately. Gorge-ous Grub cupola painted before brush acted up.
PLA or resin kits with separate roofs. Silver Ridge residential. First major airbrush targets.

Fault protection scheme for 9 wiring zones. Wired in series with isolated track sections. Self-resetting, illuminate to identify fault location. Install as each zone is wired rather than retrofitting later.

acquisitions.item: Turn of the Century Town 3D model collection
acquisitions.contents: 9 shops, blacksmith, sheriff/jail, two banks, school, unnamed building, farmhouse, barn, general store, city hall. Kit format with separate parts (windows, pillars, fencing, second floors, roofs). Era-appropriate, consistent scale and aesthetic across the set.
acquisitions.notes: More buildings than Silver Ridge needs - overflow candidates for Pine Valley Junction. Kit format ideal for airbrush painting before assembly. Fine details (window mullions, porch pillars, fence pickets) may be fragile at N scale. Blacksmith fits Silver Ridge working-town character well. Cohesive single-designer set ensures consistent scale and aesthetic on street scenes.

workflow.topo_map_note: Topo/contour work is token-intensive. Use V10_elevations JPG as primary data source - it has all connection elevations and contour labels. Do NOT use the OBJ terrain mesh. Ask Jake rather than infer/guess for anything not visible in the annotated image. Mine branch in PVJ valley is on a viaduct - its track elevations (0.87, 1.39) are NOT terrain surface points; terrain below stays at 0.0 until mountain rises to meet track. v4 topo script (srrx_topo.py) uses RBF interpolation with dense background grid + post-process clamp. Regenerate from script rather than re-deriving from scratch.

confirmed_terrain_elevations.north_leg_mainline_W_to_E: 0 → 0.1 (several) → 0.14 → 0.17 → 0.31 → 0.45. Grades: 1.9% and 2.0% on approach to mountain.
confirmed_terrain_elevations.mine_branch: 3% grade from yard turnout to smelter junction. Connections: 0.87 (intermediate, viaduct section), 1.39 (viaduct crossing Pine River - track only, terrain below is 0.0). Smelter junction: 3.04. Switchbacks: 3.1 → 3.4 → 3.51 → 3.7 (×3 on tails) → 4 → 4.4 → 4.75 smelter / 4.78 mine.
confirmed_terrain_elevations.mine_branch_viaduct_note: Mine branch is elevated above PVJ valley floor from yard to where mountain rises to meet it. Does not affect terrain contours in that section.
confirmed_terrain_elevations.east_leg_portals: Inner tunnel bore: 0.91. Outer tunnel bore: 1.13. Track climbs from portals southward to 2.0-2.29 level.
confirmed_terrain_elevations.gorge: Elk River flows south in valley (still at 2.0) then hits east-west fault and turns hard west. Fault/turn point: ~0.0. Gorge floor going west: -0.5 → -1.0 → -1.4 → -1.7 → -2.0 → -2.5 at layout exit. Timberline Lumber branch crosses river at ~2.0 (simple crossing, not gorge). Bridge/flagstop (Gorge-ous Grub) at gorge crossing where mainline crosses the E-W gorge channel.
confirmed_terrain_elevations.water_features: Moose Lake: 5.5 (glacial cirque, NE corner). Mill Pond: 3.15 (on mountain face near Timberline Lumber, fed by waterfall cascade from Moose Lake). Pine River: carved below datum, ~-0.35 channel.
confirmed_terrain_elevations.mountain_contours: 2.5 (base) → 3.0 → 4.0 → 4.5 → 5.0 → 5.5 (Moose Lake). Peak: ~6.0 planned (TBD as terrain is built - headwall above cirque).

current_state.track_plan_note: V10 supersedes V9 (2026-06-01). Smelter relocated from east leg to mine branch on north leg - now on teal spur off mine branch before first switchback. Removes implausible cross-mountain ore transit. One turnout removed north of gorge (used for smelter branch instead). Inner tunnel run adjusted, first switchback tail lengthened, mountain contours reworked. Operating sequence: empties up switchbacks to mine, full cars descend, helper waiting at smelter turnout, both engines push full load up 3.7% grade to smelter (stub spur, no runaround - no room at elevation). Both engines return light to yard. Slag pile planned on south side of smelter - downslope toward gorge, geologically honest. Slag predates Elk River National Park; creates intentional visual tension between industrial operation and park boundary. Room layout zones also documented in V10 full plan.
current_state.foam_plan: North leg: 1" foam as subroadbed base. This is operational zero. Pine River carved down into foam - river sits below grade naturally. East leg: 3" total (1"+2" stacked) to maintain 2" elevation above north leg zero. Foam in hand: one 4x8 sheet of 2", one 4x8 sheet of 1". Additional 1" sheet needed - single sheets insufficient to cover both legs at required thickness.
